about: Travel scenes for the Trip tab. Each scene has signs to recognise, lines to say, lines you will hear from staff or announcements, and a role-play. Spaces mark word breaks; every word is in lex or the glossary.

scenes.title: Convenience store
scenes.blurb: Buying food and drinks, and the questions the cashier always asks.

signs.note: Hung on shop and restaurant doors.
Common on restaurants before opening and between lunch and dinner.
Its partner is 出口, exit. 口 is mouth, an opening.
Everywhere: shops, stations, car parks.
On doors, often as a small sticker by the handle.
The other side of the door from 押.
Above the till. Also what you say to ask for the bill in a restaurant.
On price tags. This is what you actually pay.
The smaller price: you pay about 10% more at the till.
Often with a number: 3割引 is 30% off.
Stickers on bento and bread late in the evening.
Also written トイレ.

scenes.title: Trains
scenes.blurb: Tickets, platforms, transfers and the announcements on board.

signs.note: On signs pointing the way, and after station names: 新宿駅 is Shinjuku Station.
Where you tap your IC card in and out.
Where you buy tickets or top up an IC card.
Signs to other lines. Often orange or with the line's colour.
Shown after a number: 3番線 is platform 3.
Stops at every station. Sometimes shortened to 各停 or 普通.
Skips some smaller stations. Check it stops at yours.
Skips more stations than 快速 on most lines.
Usually around midnight. Miss it and it's a taxi.
Big stations have many exits. 西口 is the west exit.
For elderly, pregnant or injured people. Phones on silent here.
By the gates. Pay the difference if your ticket or card is short.

say.t: 新宿 まで いくら です か 。

say.t: 切符 を なくしました 。

scenes.title: Eating out
scenes.blurb: Getting a table, ordering, and paying on the way out.

signs.note: On doors and tables. 喫煙 means smoking is allowed.
Smoking is often only allowed in these marked areas.
A main dish with rice, miso soup and pickles. Usually the best value at lunch.
Buy a ticket at the machine by the door, then hand it over. Common in ramen and noodle shops.
Often free or about ¥100 more.
Every seat is taken. Wait, or come back later.
On a card on the table. Don't sit there.
Also written テイクアウト.
Usually with a time limit, often 90 minutes.
Common at izakaya, often as part of a set course.
Still common in small restaurants. Carry some yen.
On a board by the door or at the counter.

scenes.title: Hotel
scenes.blurb: Checking in and out, leaving bags, and finding the bath and breakfast.

signs.note: In hotels, hospitals and museums: the desk to go to first.
A shared hot bath. Wash at the showers first, and keep your towel out of the water.
Usually a blue curtain. Baths sometimes swap sides by day, so check each time.
Usually a red curtain.
An open-air hot bath, often the best part of a ryokan.
Signs point the way. Bring your room key or breakfast ticket.
On lift signs pointing to the room floors.
On safes and lockers: keep valuables here.
On key cards and room doors.
On a door or at the bath. Come back later.
The light cotton robe in your room. Fine to wear around the hotel; wrap left over right.
After a number: 3階 is the third floor. 地下 is the basement.
